answer: Inter-arrival jitter floor. Each identity’s request timing must show a minimum variance, like a gale scattering arrivals, so a scripted clone emitting at a fixed cadence is throttled. The cost is added latency per identity: an attacker must inject random delays or parallel wastes, since smooth traffic flags as one ivory-smooth stream. Identities whose timing variance stays below the ocean-wide population median get queued last, raising the attacker’s per-clone delay from milliseconds to seconds.
